    Positive definiteness of 2I - Adj(Δ) #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 2: "For M = 2I - Adj(Δ), direct expansion gives, for any real vector z, zᵀMz = ∑_{{i,j}} n_i n_j (z_i/n_i - z_j/n_j)² + ∑_i ((Mn)_i/n_i) z_i². Thus M is positive definite."

    qform G z = ∑_i 2 z_i² - ∑_i ∑_{j ∼ i} z_i z_j is zᵀ M z. If n > 0 and Mn > 0 componentwise, then qform G z > 0 for z ≠ 0 (qform_pos). For a vector z ≥ 0 supported on a configuration of edges, qform is bounded above by the same expression over the configuration (qform_le_of_pattern); this is how the forbidden subtrees are excluded.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
